title: The AI Ledger
introduction: The last complete week in AI models and coding harnesses: October 26–November 1, 2026. Coverage focuses on Codex, Claude Code, Copilot and OpenCode, with historical context and a forecast for November 2–8. Older unconfirmed reporting is explicitly marked as a carry-over watch item. Confidence is qualitative, not a calibrated probability. Daily supplements through November 4, 19:58 UTC cover separately dated model and coding-harness updates, including Preview features and a conditional acquisition announcement. These additions sit outside the reporting week; the frozen archive and original November 2–8 forecast are preserved.

items.title: Daily update · Nov 4: VS Code previews mixed-harness sessions
items.summary: VS Code 1.145 adds a preview that groups Copilot, Claude and Codex chats within one session, with separate model, agent and permission settings. The stable release also adds cron schedules and workspace custom agents for local automations.
items.whyItMatters: Developers can compare agents without splitting related conversations across separate sessions. Mixed-harness sessions require the preview setting; cron schedules do not apply to cloud automations.
items.confidenceReason: Microsoft's official release notes establish the features and their preview limits. No independent productivity improvement is claimed.
items.historicalContext: Previously, nested sessions inherited their parent's harness. This changes session organization rather than introducing a new underlying model.

sources.title: Visual Studio Code 1.145 release notes
sources.authenticityReason: Official notes explicitly date the stable release November 4, 2026 and mark mixed-harness nested sessions as Preview.

items.title: Daily update · Nov 4: Claude Code adds per-fork effort controls
items.summary: Claude Code 2.1.318 lets a mod's model fork choose its own reasoning effort, independently of the session. It also exposes stored sign-in expiry in command-line status and JSON output, with advance warnings for unattended text runs.
items.whyItMatters: Small delegated jobs can use lower effort without changing the main session. Expiry visibility gives developers a clearer signal before unattended jobs lose authentication.
items.confidenceReason: Anthropic's official release notes confirm the changes; their effect on cost and reliability was not independently measured.
items.historicalContext: This adds control at the individual mod-fork level. The same release fixes conversation continuation and idle-compaction failures.

items.title: Daily update · Nov 4: Tencent announces Hy4, with weights still to come
items.summary: Tencent's November 4 announcement describes Hy4's visual understanding and computer-use capabilities, and availability across its products. Vercel had already announced Hy4 access through AI Gateway on November 3, including image input and a one-million-token context window.
items.whyItMatters: API availability and downloadable weights are different milestones. Tencent says model weights and system cards will arrive in the coming days; the announcement does not establish that they are available now.
items.confidenceReason: A Tencent-issued announcement and Vercel's own integration changelog support the availability claims. Performance descriptions remain vendor-reported.
items.historicalContext: Hy4 follows Hy4 Preview. November 3 gateway access and November 4 corporate announcement are distinct dates, not two separate model launches.

items.title: Daily update · Nov 4: OpenAI announces plans to acquire Pierre
items.summary: OpenAI says it will acquire Pierre, the developer-tools company behind Code Storage. Closing remains subject to customary conditions and regulatory approvals; the companies remain independent until then.
items.whyItMatters: The planned acquisition could bring source-control and code-review tools more closely into Codex. It is not a completed transaction or an announcement that new integrations are available today.
items.confidenceReason: The official announcement establishes the stated plan and closing conditions, not a guaranteed closing date or delivered product roadmap.
items.historicalContext: Pierre’s Trees and Diffs libraries already support file browsing and code review in the Codex app. The announcement builds on that existing relationship.

items.title: Daily update · Nov 3: Claude Code adds fail-closed hook controls
items.summary: Claude Code 2.1.317 adds an Agent SDK hook option that blocks an action if its callback fails, warnings about unexpected connectors on scheduled cloud tasks, and checks before web or shell calls transmit the account email address.
items.whyItMatters: These controls affect how coding agents handle failures and external actions. The release also adds a gateway-admin cost report, with spend grouped by date, developer or identity-provider group.
items.confidenceReason: Official release notes establish the announced changes. They do not independently prove that every failure or unintended transmission is prevented.
items.historicalContext: The October 31 release added subagent-effort and pooled-budget controls. November 3 extends operational oversight with hook-failure handling and cost reporting.

items.title: Daily update · Nov 3: Copilot arrives in JetBrains Air
items.summary: GitHub announced Copilot integration in JetBrains Air through Agent Client Protocol. Developers can track parallel sessions and review changes in context, using their Copilot subscription for local or cloud coding tasks.
items.whyItMatters: Cloud use requires an Air Teams-enabled business organization and administrator enablement. Tasks use Copilot rather than JetBrains AI credits; Air analytics do not show Copilot usage, and Air cannot set its spending limits.
items.confidenceReason: GitHub's dated first-party announcement describes availability and limitations. Access still depends on account, subscription and administrator settings.
items.historicalContext: After GitHub's October 28 connected-cloud rollout, this adds a JetBrains Air entry point. The new integration is distinct from the existing Copilot plugin.

items.title: Daily update · Nov 2: LongCat-2.5 reaches the API
items.summary: LongCat's official API changelog marks LongCat-2.5 available on November 2, following a November 1 announcement. The company positions it for visual understanding and long-running coding tasks, and lists compatibility with Claude Code, Codex and Hermes.
items.whyItMatters: A new model can enter existing coding workflows without a wholly new harness. Compatibility is the vendor's claim, not evidence that every setup works unchanged or that it outperforms alternatives.
items.confidenceReason: Official dated API documentation establishes the availability announcement. Capability and harness-compatibility claims remain vendor-reported and were not independently tested here.
items.historicalContext: The same changelog dates LongCat-2.5-Preview to September 25. The full-model blog is dated November 1; the API availability entry is November 2. This is a preview-to-release progression, not two separate model launches.

items.title: GPT-6.1 Terra rolls out
items.summary: OpenAI announced Terra for its API, ChatGPT Work and Codex—not Chat. Listed standard API prices are $1 per million input tokens and $5 per million output tokens.
items.whyItMatters: Teams have another deployment option; they should test quality on their own workloads instead of treating price as a capability ranking.
items.confidenceReason: Official release documentation establishes the announcement and listed terms, not independent comparative performance.
items.historicalContext: GPT-4o mini's July 2024 launch also emphasized cost-efficient deployment. Different capability classes make raw token-price comparisons misleading.

items.title: Codex CLI 0.165 adds Terra and more session control
items.summary: The October 27 release adds GPT-6.1 Terra to model catalogs, a built-in Google Cloud Vertex AI provider, repository filtering, and in-conversation reasoning-effort changes for supported models.
items.whyItMatters: The harness is changing alongside the model: provider choice and session organization affect how coding work actually runs.
items.confidenceReason: High confidence in the published release announcement; rollout and configuration can vary. No independent productivity gain is claimed.
items.historicalContext: The preceding 0.164 release on October 23 added reusable prompt presets and inline model/permission controls. These are successive workflow changes, not evidence of a benchmark jump.

items.title: Copilot connects coding sessions across surfaces
items.summary: GitHub announced a connected cloud experience on paid Copilot plans. Sessions can continue across web, mobile, CLI, app and VS Code, with cloud sandboxes and shared Actions compute entitlement.
items.whyItMatters: Session continuity and execution environments are becoming central product features. GitHub says sandbox usage billing begins in November; teams should check their entitlement.
items.confidenceReason: High confidence in the published release announcement; rollout and configuration can vary. No independent productivity gain is claimed.
items.historicalContext: GitHub describes this as a connected successor to its separate Copilot Chat and coding-agent experiences. The shift is from isolated surfaces toward resumable work.

items.title: OpenCode 2.2.5 improves compaction and worktree controls
items.summary: The October 30 release adds percentage-based context buffers, worktree/base-branch shortcuts, and fixes for context-window errors and model-switch reasoning handling.
items.whyItMatters: A buffer expressed as a percentage can adapt across model context sizes. These are concrete harness ergonomics and reliability changes, not a new underlying model.
items.confidenceReason: High confidence in the published release announcement; rollout and configuration can vary. No independent productivity gain is claimed.
items.historicalContext: Previously the buffer setting accepted a token count; percentage support makes one configuration more portable across differently sized model windows.

items.title: Claude Code adds subagent effort and budget controls
items.summary: Claude Code 2.1.316 adds a default subagent-effort setting and pooled group budgets in the Claude apps gateway. It also fixes shell processes left running when Claude Code exits itself.
items.whyItMatters: Teams can control delegated work more explicitly. Gateway-specific budget features should not be confused with universal personal-plan controls.
items.confidenceReason: High confidence in the published release announcement; rollout and configuration can vary. No independent productivity gain is claimed.
items.historicalContext: The release changes the previous default of subagents inheriting session effort when no other setting names one. It illustrates increasingly granular agent orchestration.

items.title: Next week: another control upgrade in a coding harness
items.summary: Editorial forecast for November 2–8: at least one of Codex, Copilot, OpenCode or Claude Code will announce a new session, context-management, or subagent-control feature.
items.whyItMatters: Model capability alone is not the whole developer experience. Worktree continuity, context management and delegated-work controls are actionable dimensions to evaluate.
items.confidenceReason: The last complete week contains relevant releases from all four projects. That supports a modest directional forecast, but provides neither a calibrated probability nor a promised roadmap. Progress check, November 3: GitHub’s official Air integration announcement adds parallel-session tracking, which appears to meet the session-organization criterion. This is an interim assessment, not a changed forecast or an early formal resolution. The original November 8 resolution time still applies. November 4 follow-up: Claude Code 2.1.318 adds individual mod-fork effort controls, providing further interim evidence for delegated-work controls. Formal resolution remains scheduled after November 8, as originally specified.
items.historicalContext: October brought Codex session filtering, Copilot cloud continuity, OpenCode context-buffer controls, and Claude Code subagent-effort settings. The forecast extrapolates this observed cluster without assuming every vendor follows it.
